title: The cost of a defect across the lifecycle: why finding it early is cheaper

videos.script: Every testing course shows the same chart. A defect costs one to fix in the requirements, and a hundred after release. {{chart}} The shape is right. The numbers are shakier than the slides suggest. {{shaky}} The hundred came from large projects in the nineteen seventies. The same paper that repeats it says that for small systems, five to one is closer. {{five}} So this lesson argues from the mechanism instead. {{mechanism}} Four things grow while a defect waits. What is built on top of it. Who has met it. Who still remembers why. And how many steps the fix must pass through. {{four}} Then you count one. A short program sells a month of tickets through the cinema's price rule. {{program}} And it tells you exactly how many pensioners paid too much. {{count}} That number is the floor of the cost, not the whole of it. {{end}}
